spd_hint: HPS + LED mixed (LED CCT unknown, likely 3000-4000K)
notes: Greater Santiago is ~35+ comunas each running its own lighting, so there is no single city stock. Comuna de Santiago (the centre): 37,054 luminaires; plan announced Nov 2020 to replace 23,500 (63%) old sodium with LED by 1H-2021; earlier LED on Alameda/Vicuna Mackenna/Matta/San Francisco in 2017 and Barrio Yungay in 2019; GORE RM put in 4,191 LED in Santiago Centro (Jan 2019). So the comuna de Santiago is probably mostly LED since 2021, but no completion figure was found. Nationally, the BID 2013 inventory in the DIPRES evaluation gives ~2.42M luminaires, 77-89% HPS. The national MinEnergia recambio programme started Aug 2014 (85 comunas, 130,000 luminaires by 2017, target 200,000) and was aimed at poorer comunas. NASA Earth Observatory (ISS070-E-93399, 14 Feb 2024) shows a patchwork of orange HPS and white LED across comunas and says Maipu and El Bosque began changing lights in autumn 2023, so the metro area is still mixed. No tender or press release that states a CCT was found; the Providencia (2020) and Las Condes (2025) tender bases exist but their CCT could not be read. Regulation: DS 43/2012 covered only the observatory regions (Antofagasta, Atacama, Coquimbo; from background knowledge, not checked this session), so it did not bind Santiago. DS 1/2022 (published 18 Oct 2023, in force 19 Oct 2024) covers the whole country: outside Special Protection Areas the blue-light share is capped at 7% (1% inside them). Existing national-territory installations only need to comply at end of useful life, and new ones from 19 Oct 2026. So post-2024 installs should be warm (~3000K or lower) and pre-2024 LED may be 4000K. led_share and cct left blank on purpose.

BHIP PPP: 20-year contract (Jun 2017 to 2037); 182,257 sodium-vapour points to be replaced with LED; service order May 2017, works from Jul 2017. 120,000 were LED by Nov 2019 (~66%); PBH said in Mar 2022 that more than 180,000 points were modernised 'in just three years', so ~100% LED around 2020-21. Telemanagement on ~32,800 points. The PBH Ativos summary of the contract gives only a minimum average IRC of 65, no CCT. The contract annexes PDF (pbhativos.com.br/.../Contrato-da-PPP_Iluminacao-Publica_Anexos.pdf) is over 10 MB, too big for the fetch tool, so its CCT clause was not read. 4000K is inferred from the contemporaneous Sao Paulo PPP spec (4000 +/-300K standard) and common 2016-18 Brazilian PPP practice; check the annex before relying on it. The new 'Ilumina BH' programme adds 25,000 luminaires to 2028.

The PPP Anexo VI (Caderno de Encargos da Concessionaria) specifies LED luminaires with 'Temperatura de cor: 4000 +/- 300 K', 5000 +/-300K or 3000 +/-300K allowed only exceptionally with municipal approval; also IRC >=70 and >=100 lm/W. It says the existing network is predominantly sodium vapour. The file name suggests an early (2014-15) edital version and the edital was republished several times, so the signed 2018 annex could differ. Contract signed 8 Mar 2018 with Iluminacao Paulista SPE (CLD, Lacos, FM Rodrigues); modernisation under the PPP from Aug 2019; ongoing litigation. Progress: 186,387 points modernised plus 8,613 new by 16 Dec 2020. PMSP press release of 8 Oct 2021 says 'mais de 600 mil pontos de luz de LED ... 90% do total' of more than 630k points. That jump from 186k in ten months looks implausible and may be a misstatement, so treat the 90% (2021) as unverified. Target was full LED by 2024; completion not confirmed (web-search budget ran out).

2013 contract: 'gestion integral y energetica de instalaciones urbanas', 3 lots, 8 years from 1 Jan 2014, EUR 772M total, ESE model. Lots 1-2 went to UTE Luz Madrid (Sice, Urbalux, Imesapi, Etralux, Citelum) and lot 3 to UTE Inmaes (Ferrovial, FCC, Indra, Telvent). Retrofit Q4 2014 to 1H 2015 (~150,000 done by Mar 2015) covered 225,000 points. 84,000 became Philips LED: 33,000 historic 'Fernandino/Villa' lanterns got LED modules made in Valladolid, and 51,000 1990s globe luminaires were replaced with 'Quebec' LED. The other ~124,000-141,000 points only got a more efficient light source and electronic gear. The UCM thesis/paper (Robles et al. 2021) describes this as HPS 250 W/150 W reduced to 150 W/70 W, i.e. HPS kept at lower wattage. A programmed night-time power-reduction schedule plus GPRS telemanagement was also part of the design. Target was 44% lighting energy saving. The '3000 K' figure comes from a search snippet attributed to Robles et al. 2021 ('retrofits in Madrid primarily replace HPS lamps with 3000 K LEDs'). I could not open the full text (MDPI 403; the Zenodo PDF was too large), so it is snippet-only. UCM also measured HPS, 3000K and 4000K LED spectra on Madrid street poles. LED share: 35.6% in 2019 and 66.9% in 2025 out of 253,575 luminaires. 2019 matches the 84k LED installed in 2015, so there was little LED growth 2015-2019. 2022 maintenance contract: more than 71,000 discharge luminaires to LED; target at least 75% LED by 2027 (PRTR funds). Ground truth: UCM sky brightness in Johnson B fell 14% 2011-2015 and rose 32% 2015-2019. Spain's REEAE (RD 1890/2008) sets efficiency and upward-light limits, not CCT. The 2013 PPT pliego on sede.madrid.es returned 403.
